requirement_text.REQ-395:
Deploy SwiftRoute's sequential high-value shipment-approval ProcessDefinition as a live, browsable definition on a real tenant on QA.
AC1: ProcessDefinition exists live on QA, confirmed via definitions-list API.
AC2: Instance with declared_value: 750 → pending ops-review task, then pending ceo-approval task.
AC3: Instance with declared_value: 400 → no ceo-approval task at all.
AC4: [DEFERRED to after ISS-0739]

task.description:
Execute Step 2a (Backend Implementation) for REQ-395.

QA URL: https://qa.bizdala.com

This is a DEPLOYMENT requirement, not a typical code change. The implementation is:
1. Write scripts/seed_swiftroute_definition.sh -- the idempotent curl script per the design doc
2. Attempt to execute the script against QA and verify ACs 1-3
3. If QA prerequisites are missing (no swiftroute tenant, no auth token), document what is blocked and why

PROCEDURE:

1. Verify branch: git branch --show-current must equal feature/WF02-REQ395-20260924

2. Read lib/letflow/design/req395-swiftroute-definition-deployment.md fully before writing anything.

3. Check QA state prerequisites:
   a. Check deploy/ for any QA auth token configuration or admin credentials
   b. Check scripts/ for any existing seed/deploy scripts that show the auth pattern
   c. Look for any documented QA admin account (check README.md, docs/, deploy/)
   d. Try GET https://qa.bizdala.com/api/v1/health or /health to confirm QA is reachable
   e. If you find a QA admin auth token: proceed with deployment
   f. If no auth token can be found from the codebase: write the script anyway with a clear TOKEN placeholder, document this as a blocker, and report PARTIAL

4. Write scripts/seed_swiftroute_definition.sh per §1 and §2 of the design doc:
   - The full ProcessDefinition payload from §2.1
   - Idempotency guard (check if definition already exists)
   - Two-step creation: POST /api/v1/definitions → POST /api/v1/definitions/{id}/activate
   - Make it executable (chmod +x equivalent in git)
   - Include usage/prereqs comment at the top

5. If QA auth token is available:
   a. Execute the seed script against QA
   b. Verify AC1: fetch via definitions-list API, quote the response
   c. Verify AC2: submit instance with declared_value: 750, quote the response showing ops-review task pending
      - If completing ops-review requires a user with role-ops-manager (blocked by ISS-0739): submit the instance and verify the ops-review task appears; document the ceo-approval step as blocked by ISS-0739
   d. Verify AC3: submit instance with declared_value: 400, quote the response showing NO ceo-approval task
   e. Quote all responses verbatim in your handoff

6. mix compile --warnings-as-errors (even if no .ex files changed, confirm clean compile)

7. git add scripts/seed_swiftroute_definition.sh
8. git commit -m 'feat(REQ-395): seeding script for swiftroute ProcessDefinition on QA'

9. Complete your handoff (step-02a-elixir-dev.json):
   - Status COMPLETED
   - result.status: PASS if all feasible ACs verified; PARTIAL if blocked by ISS-0739 or missing QA credentials; FAIL if the script is wrong or deployment errors
   - result.ac_results: what was verified for each AC
   - result.blockers: list anything that prevented full verification
   - next_action: 'Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c)' on PASS/PARTIAL

NOTE: A PARTIAL result where AC1 and AC3 pass but AC2's ceo-approval step is blocked by ISS-0739 is an EXPECTED and ACCEPTABLE outcome for this requirement -- the requirement text itself says ISS-0739 must land for end-to-end exercise. Report it plainly.
